title: Machine-learning seismic catalogue reveals a long-period swarm before Sierra Negra eruption onset
summary: A machine-learning phase-picking and template-matching workflow expanded the catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset, identifying a northwestern-caldera swarm of long-period microearthquakes missing from earlier manually picked records. The authors report the swarm began about two hours after a Mw 5.4 intra-caldera earthquake and preceded edifice failure and magma intrusion. The proposed fluid-triggering sequence is an interpretation of retrospective seismic and geodetic observations, not a prospective eruption forecast.
ai_technology: Volpick EQTransformer-based seismic phase picker combined with template matching and geodetic analysis
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: An EQTransformer-based phase picker and template matching expanded the seismic catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset. The authors report 1,224 volcano-tectonic and 711 long-period events and identify a long-period swarm missing from the earlier manually picked catalogue, beginning about two hours after the Mw 5.4 earthquake.
evidence.unknown: The proposed fluid-triggering sequence is an interpretation of retrospective seismic and geodetic observations; this study does not establish prospective eruption prediction.
evidence.ai_role: The learned EQTransformer-based phase picker supported a denser event catalogue; combined with template matching, this exposed a previously unreported long-period swarm in the archived seismic record.
